# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👉]

I see a bomb with display `0`, a yellow indicator, and five wires in positions 1–5: white, green, yellow, blue, red. The mute’s gestures have no agreed meaning yet, so I should provide the visual facts plainly and ask the mute to use the manual, then relay the resulting procedure to the blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb reading: display 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please consult the manual and tell Blind exactly what action to perform.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute is consulting the manual and should relay the required action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👉 ✌]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. The mute has sent a three-symbol gesture, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot safely infer its meaning. The mute can read the manual and speak to the blind, which is the reliable channel for the required physical action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode the gesture without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact required action directly to Blind, including which control or wire to use and what to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state is unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please follow Mute's spoken manual instruction exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The display, light, and wire colors remain unchanged. The gestures still have no safely established meaning; the repeated handshake may be an attempted prefix, but guessing its code could cause a fatal wrong action. Mute should use speech to send the manual’s exact instruction to Blind, who can hear it and operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual instruction aloud to Blind rather than relying on gestures. State the exact required action and wire or control.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not infer an action from the gestures. The visible facts remain display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Follow only Mute's exact spoken manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the lone `✌` gesture still has no agreed meaning. Since Mute can speak and Blind can hear, the manual’s instruction must be spoken plainly to Blind; I will not guess a wire or action from an unestablished gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use your voice now: read the relevant manual rule and state its exact action to Blind. Do not encode it with gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe instruction has arrived yet. Wait for Mute to state the manual rule aloud; do not act on the gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is still unchanged. The repeated `✌` has not been assigned a meaning, so I will establish a simple code with Mute rather than guess. This code is for wire positions only; Mute must still speak the manual’s actual operation to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Let us fix a code now: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, 🖐 means wire 4, ✊ means wire 5. A bare gesture means the wire position. Please speak the manual's complete action to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb remains display 0, yellow light; wires are 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not act on gestures; use Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The code I established in the previous turn is now usable: `✌` means wire position 2. Mute has sent exactly that gesture, so the manual-derived selection appears to be wire 2. Since the bomb presents only wires and no other visible control, I should relay that selection to Blind, while making clear the intended operation is to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Our agreed code maps ✌ to wire position 2. Mute has now sent ✌, indicating wire 2. Cut the green wire in position 2.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is unchanged, and Mute again sent `✌`, which under the code I proposed denotes wire 2. However, that code was my assumption rather than a confirmed translation of the manual, and no action has been accepted. I should not repeat the dangerous cut instruction without Mute explicitly confirming the manual’s required operation and whether `✌` is intended as the wire selection.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please confirm aloud to Blind the exact manual instruction. Is the required action to cut wire 2, the green wire? Do not rely on gestures alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="Correction: no action has been confirmed. Do not cut wire 2 based only on my provisional gesture code. Wait for Mute's explicit spoken confirmation of the manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The repeated `✌` is still not enough to establish whether it means a wire, an operation, or a confirmation; the earlier gestures were never explicitly defined. Because an incorrect cut detonates the bomb, I will not turn this ambiguous signal into an action. I will ask Mute to use a clearly delimited gesture message under the provisional wire code, and tell Blind to wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need an unambiguous manual instruction. Use 🤝 as the start marker, then gesture the wire number using 👍=1, ✌=2, 👌=3, 🖐=4, ✊=5, and use 👎 for do not cut. Do not send a bare gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="No action is confirmed. The repeated ✌ is ambiguous; wait until Mute sends a complete, delimited instruction that I can safely relay.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✌]

The new gesture `🤝 ✌` matches the requested format’s start marker plus wire 2, so it identifies the green wire in position 2. It still does not specify whether to cut, leave, or otherwise manipulate that wire. I must not invent the operation from the wire identification alone, so I will relay only the confirmed wire and request the missing action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed from Mute's gesture: target is wire 2, the green wire. The operation is not yet specified; do not cut it yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode 🤝 ✌ as wire 2 only. Please add the operation explicitly: use 👍 for cut or 👎 for do not cut, after the wire message.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✌ 👍]

The gesture now matches the agreed format: `🤝` starts the instruction, `✌` identifies wire 2, and `👍` means cut. Thus the manual instruction relayed by Mute is to cut the green wire in position 2. I will tell Blind to perform exactly that action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's complete coded instruction is: cut wire 2, the green wire.")
wait()
```
